SAF provides a near-term solution to reducing aviation emissions, which represented 9% of U.S. transportation emissions in 2022 (EPA 2025b). SAF is a commercial fuel that has been in use since 2016. The SAF Grand Challenge is a joint initiative of DOE, the U.S. Department of Transportation, and USDA that seeks to expand U.S. production and reduce costs. The near-term goal is to increase SAF production to 3 billion gallons per year by 2030, and the long-term goal is 100% SAF at 35 billion gallons by 2050 (DOE n.d.). R&D is heavily focused on improving technology pathway efficiency to reduce costs and increase production. ASTM D7566, Standard Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuel Containing Synthesized Hydrocarbons, dictates fuel quality standards for non-petroleum-based jet fuel and outlines approved SAF-based fuel production pathways and the percentage allowable in a blend with Jet A. There are currently eight synthetic paraffinic kerosene, synthetic kerosene with aromatics, and other approved pathways (Table 3). ASTM D1655, Standard Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuels, allows coprocessing of non-petroleum feedstocks at petroleum refineries at a rate of up to 5% and up to 10% for HEFA biointermediates. Blending limits are shown in Table 3.
